method.advancement: A supplement needs at least two added useful locations across at least two generator families, at most one additional ordinary source group per held panel and no additional isolated-background flags.
method.arms: Compare conventional dense frame responses and signed input contributions separately. The agreement arm keeps a dense window only if its contribution is at least the median among measured windows in that same recording.
method.contribution: Take the derivative of the full context's pre-sigmoid mean frame response with respect to its normalized Mel input. For each time position, multiply the gradient by the input and sum the signed terms from the upper 40 of 80 bands in both Mel frames. Multiply by the number of feature positions to cancel mean pooling's length factor. The lower bands stay fixed. This estimates local sensitivity to drawing the upper bands toward the context-average Mel input.
method.geometry: Use the established one-second windows at half-second steps. Use the native 280+320k sample centers, at least 40 measured frames, the median signed term in each window, and the lower result when both contexts qualify.
method.input: Use the unchanged primary mixture and speech gate. Use original waveform conditioning, normalized Mel features and the frozen voice model over two four-second contexts at zero and two seconds.
method.point: Use the larger of the second-highest previously unflagged ordinary development group maximum and the highest previously unflagged isolated-background maximum for each arm. Apply strictly. Preserve current flags in supplement comparisons. A useful position covers at least half the labeled edit and reaches 0.30 time IoU.
